character_facts: Lothar is described as a warrior who avoids fighting alone and uses the environment strategically.
Tonto is trusted enough to be asked to inspect circuits for evidence about Steelhead.
Steelhead's survival is uncertain and is the subject of the current test.
Aghnar's victory status is disputed by the speakers on the page.
One robot speaker admits to having shown too little faith in Tonto.

continuity_links: The page continues an ongoing conflict involving Lothar, Aghnar, Steelhead, and the Phagureans.
The outcome of a prior battle remains contested, and the present technical examination seems intended to resolve who survived or won.
The imagery of sealed chambers and circuit testing suggests continuation from an earlier rescue, autopsy, or recovery sequence.
dialogue_meaning: A speaker uses Lothar's actions as a lesson in warrior strategy: he survives by using the terrain, specifically the acid lake, as an advantage.
A robot apologizes for doubting Tonto.
Technical voices report that the bio-electrogram is dissolving the target and that the meca-womb has been sealed.
A completed test is said to offer a way to determine whether Steelhead survived, if Tonto can find the relevant circuits.
Another speaker rejects the possibility of the proposed outcome, arguing that an Aghnar victory would have led to total human extinction.
A final voice angrily insists that Aghnar had already been declared the winner.
locations: A hazardous lakeside environment described as an acid lake
An interior or mechanical chamber containing the meca-womb
A capsule or medical/containment area with enclosed bodies or energy structures
lore_facts: The setting includes an 'acid lake' dangerous enough to be used tactically in combat.
A process called a 'bio-electrogram' can dissolve a living or biomechanical structure.
A structure called a 'meca-womb' exists and can be sealed during a technical procedure.
Circuit analysis is treated as a way to determine whether Steelhead survived.
The Phagureans are described as a force that would eliminate humanity if Aghnar had truly won.
plot_events: A violent reaction or detonation occurs near an acid lake or similar hazardous terrain.
An organic structure identified as a 'meca-womb' is dissolved by a 'bio-electrogram.'
The meca-womb is then reported sealed.
A speaker claims a test is complete and asks Tonto to identify which circuits would indicate whether Steelhead survived.
Another speaker argues this is impossible because, if Aghnar had won the battle, the Phagureans would have eradicated the human race and history would be different.
A boastful voice insists Aghnar was the winner.
The page ends on images of an enclosed human figure, an energy-webbed chamber, and a robot face, emphasizing uncertainty about survival and outcome.

visual_summary: A bright explosion or chemical reaction erupts across the top of the page beside a sleek black craft or projectile. Below, a bulbous organic mass dissolves in a foaming blue liquid while the black craft dives past it. Small robots speak from off-panel or lower panels, reporting a successful dissolution and the sealing of a 'meca-womb.' In the bottom row, a pale blue-lit human figure lies enclosed in a capsule while a web-like energy pattern fills a neighboring capsule panel; at the far right, a large robot head appears in close-up.
